C13H10O could be phenanthren-9-one? Phenanthrene is C14H10. Phenanthren-9-one would be C14H8O again. So not.

Maybe benzophenone (diphenyl ketone) C13H10O? Benzophenone formula C13H10O? Let's check: benzophenone is C13H10O (two phenyl rings attached to carbonyl). Since two rings are equivalent, total unique carbon types: carbonyl carbon (1), ipso carbon (1), ortho (1), meta (1), para (1) =5. Yes matches 5 unique carbon environments. Hydrogen environment: all aromatic hydrogens are equivalent? In benzophenone, each phenyl ring has hydrogens at ortho, meta, para positions. Are they chemically equivalent across the molecule? But the question says count unique hydrogen environments, not peaks. In benzophenone, there are 3 distinct aromatic H types. So not 1.
